_readme: Medication CLASSES, not products, and never doses.
This project does not prescribe. It describes what a class of medicine is
generally used for and what is commonly discussed with a doctor before
taking it, so a user can have a better-informed conversation. It must
never tell anyone to start, stop or change a medicine, and it never states
a dose — a test enforces both.
`allergy_keywords` are matched against the allergies on a user's profile,
so information about a class they react to is flagged rather than shown
flat. Matching is substring and deliberately loose: over-warning here is
NOT REVIEWED BY A CLINICIAN. Written from public patient-facing sources
for an educational project and must be reviewed before any real use.

analgesic.common_uses: Reducing pain and, for some, fever.
analgesic.considerations: Different pain relievers suit different people. Some affect the stomach, kidneys or liver, and some interact with blood thinners or blood pressure medicines.

antibiotic.common_uses: Treating bacterial infections. They do not work against viruses such as colds or flu.
antibiotic.considerations: A course is normally taken exactly as directed by the prescriber. Ask about interactions, and mention any previous reaction to an antibiotic before starting one.

antifungal.common_uses: Treating fungal infections of the skin, nails or elsewhere.
antifungal.considerations: Creams and tablets differ considerably in how they act and what they interact with. Oral antifungals can affect the liver, so existing liver problems are worth mentioning.

antiviral.common_uses: Treating or controlling certain viral infections.
antiviral.considerations: Often most effective when started early. Several interact with other medicines, so a full list of what you take is useful at the appointment.

antihistamine.common_uses: Relieving allergy symptoms such as itching, sneezing and rashes.
antihistamine.considerations: Some cause drowsiness and affect driving. They can interact with alcohol and with sedating medicines.

corticosteroid.common_uses: Reducing inflammation, in creams, inhalers or tablets depending on the condition.
corticosteroid.considerations: Longer courses need medical supervision and are not stopped abruptly. Ask about effects on blood sugar, bone health and infection risk.

bronchodilator.common_uses: Opening the airways in asthma and some other lung conditions.
bronchodilator.considerations: Needing a reliever more often than usual is a sign to be reviewed rather than to simply use it more. Inhaler technique changes how well it works.

antacid_ppi.common_uses: Reducing stomach acid in reflux, heartburn and ulcers.
antacid_ppi.considerations: Long-term use is normally reviewed. Some affect how other medicines are absorbed, and ongoing symptoms despite treatment are worth reporting.

antidiabetic.considerations: Doses are individual and adjusted by the prescriber. Ask what to do on days when you are unwell or eating differently, and about recognising low blood sugar.

thyroid_medicine.considerations: Doses are set from blood tests and reviewed regularly. Timing relative to food and other medicines can matter.

antihypertensive.common_uses: Lowering blood pressure and reducing cardiovascular risk.
antihypertensive.considerations: Usually taken long term even when you feel well. Ask about side effects, monitoring, and what to do if you miss a dose.

antimalarial.considerations: Which medicine is appropriate depends on where the infection was acquired. Malaria can become serious quickly and needs prompt medical care.

antitubercular.common_uses: Treating tuberculosis, normally as a combination over several months.
antitubercular.considerations: Completing the full course matters for both recovery and resistance. Regular monitoring, including liver checks, is usual.

topical_skin.common_uses: Creams, ointments and shampoos applied to the skin.
topical_skin.considerations: How much and how often varies a great deal by product and body area. Some thin the skin with prolonged use.

rehydration.common_uses: Replacing fluid and salts lost through vomiting or diarrhoea.
rehydration.considerations: Oral rehydration solutions are designed for this; plain water alone may not replace salts. Being unable to keep fluids down needs medical attention.

vaccine.common_uses: Preventing certain infections, or reducing their severity.
vaccine.considerations: Eligibility and timing depend on age, health and history. A previous reaction to a vaccine is important to mention.
